'''Edwin Vedejs''' ({{IPAc-en|v|ɛ|'|d|eɪ|z}}) ({{langx|lv|Edvīns Vedējs}}; January 31, 1941 – December 2, 2017) was a Latvian-American professor of chemistry. In 1967, he joined the organic chemistry faculty at [[University of Wisconsin]]. He rose through the ranks during his 32 years at Wisconsin being named Helfaer Professor (1991–1996) and Robert M. Bock Professor (1997–1998). In 1999, he moved to the [[University of Michigan]] and served as the [[Moses Gomberg]] Collegiate Professor of Chemistry for the final 13 years of his tenure.<ref name="orgsyn"/> He was elected a fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]] in 2011.<ref name="acs">{{Cite web |title=2011 ACS Fellows – American Chemical Society |author= |work=American Chemical Society |date= |access-date=9 May 2020 |url= https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/fellows/list-of-2011-acs-fellows.html|archivedate=22 April 2019|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20190422082952/https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/fellows/list-of-2011-acs-fellows.html}}</ref> After his retirement in 2011, the University of Michigan established the Edwin Vedejs Collegiate Professor of Chemistry Chair. Vedejs died on December 2, 2017, in [[Madison, Wisconsin]].<ref name="orgsyn">{{Cite web|url=http://www.orgsyn.org/content/pdfs/bios/evedejs.pdf|title=Edwin Vedejs 1941–2017|work=[[Organic Syntheses]]|accessdate=9 May 2020|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200509230337/http://www.orgsyn.org/content/pdfs/bios/evedejs.pdf|archivedate=9 May 2020}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Edwin "Ed" Vedejs was born in [[Riga, Latvia]] to Velta (nee Robežnieks) and Nikolajs Vedējs. Not long after his birth, the [[German occupation of Latvia during World War II]] occurred followed by the [[Soviet re-occupation of Latvia in 1944]]. These events forced his family to settle in the Fischbach Displaced Persons camp<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.archiv.org.lv/baltic_dp_germany/?id=12&lang=en|title=Camps in Germany for refugees from Baltic|website=www.archiv.org.lv}}</ref> in Germany for six years. In 1950, they emigrated to the United States and first settled in [[Fort Atkinson, WI]]. They eventually moved to [[Grand Rapids, MI]].<ref name="CHCC">{{cite journal|author=Pēteris Trapencieris|title=Edwin Vedejs (1941–2017)|journal=Chemistry of Heterocyclic Compounds|volume=53|issue=12|year=2018|pages=1373–1374|issn=0009-3122|doi=10.1007/s10593-018-2221-2|s2cid=189842530}}</ref>

He attended [[Grand Rapids Junior College]] for a few years before transferring to the University of Michigan where he received a BS degree in 1962.<ref>{{cite book|title=Michiganensian|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=N9bmAAAAMAAJ|year=1962|publisher=UM Libraries|page=470|id=UOM:39015033397756}}</ref> He moved to the University of Wisconsin and joined the group of Professor {{Interlanguage link|Hans Muxfeldt|de}} for his Ph.D. studies (''Progress toward the total synthesis of [[terramycin]]''),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=z3jVAAAAMAAJ|title=Progress Toward the Total Synthesis of Terramycin|first=Edwin|last=Vedejs|date=May 7, 1966|publisher=University of Wisconsin—Madison|via=Google Books}}</ref> which he completed in 1966. From 1966–67, he did post-doctoral research on the [[total synthesis]] of [[prostaglandins]]<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Corey EJ, Andersen NH, Carlson RM, Paust J, Vedejs E, Vlattas I, Winter RE | date = 1968 | title = Total Synthesis of Prostaglandins. Synthesis of the Pure dl-E1, -F1α, -F1β, -A1, and -B1 Hormones | journal = Journal of the American Chemical Society | volume = 90 | issue = 12 | pages = 3245–3247| doi = 10.1021/ja01014a053| pmid = 5649181 }}</ref> at [[Harvard University]] in the laboratory of [[:List of Nobel laureates in Chemistry|Nobel Laureate]] Professor [[E. J. Corey]].<ref name="wisc">{{Cite web| url=https://kb.wisconsin.edu/images/group222/shared/2018-02-05FacultySenate/2719VedejsMR.pdf |title=Memorial Resolution of the Faculty of the University of Wisconsin-Madison|work=University of Wisconsin-Madison|accessdate=9 May 2020|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200509230713/https://kb.wisconsin.edu/images/group222/shared/2018-02-05FacultySenate/2719VedejsMR.pdf|archivedate=9 May 2020}}</ref>

==Research==
[[File:Wittig_example.jpg |thumb|left|A Wittig reaction between an aldehyde and a [[phosphorane]] to give an olefin through an [[oxaphosphetane]] intermediate ]]
Vedejs' main areas of research focus included [[organic synthesis]] methodologies and reaction mechanisms. His group targeted the synthesis of several natural products, such as [[retronecine]], [[mitomycin]], and [[cytochalasin]], but the completion of a total synthesis was always secondary to the main goal of exploring new methodologies.<ref name="CHCC"/><ref name="wisc"/> His mechanistic research of the [[Wittig reaction]] revealed the importance of the [[oxaphosphetane]].<ref name="wisc"/> The application of heteroatoms such as nitrogen, sulfur, phosphorus, boron, silicon and tin were often prominently featured,<ref name="CHCC"/> which has been summarized in his self-penned account of his work.<ref>{{cite journal | title = Studies in Heteroelement-Based Synthesis | vauthors = Vedejs E | journal = The Journal of Organic Chemistry | volume = 69 | issue = 16 | pages = 5159–5167 | date = 30 July 2004 | doi = 10.1021/jo049360l| pmid = 15287757 }}</ref> Vedejs also tackled a wide range of methodologies aimed at stereoselective synthesis including protonation of carbanions, acylation and alkylation of achiral and prochiral nucleophiles, parallel kinetic resolution,<ref>{{cite journal | title = Parallel Kinetic Resolution | vauthors = Vedejs E, Chen X |journal = Journal of the American Chemical Society | volume = 119 | issue = 10 | pages = 2584–2585 | date = 12 March 1997 | doi = 10.1021/ja963666v| bibcode = 1997JAChS.119.2584V }}</ref> and control of configuration by crystallization-induced asymmetric transformation.

Over the course of his career, Vedejs published over 230 peer-reviewed articles.<ref name="wisc"/> He served as an associate editor of the ''[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]'' from 1994 to 1999, as chair of the [[NIH]] Medicinal Chemistry Study Section from 1990 to 1991, as chair of the [[American Chemical Society#Division of Organic Chemistry|Organic Division of the American Chemical Society]] in 2003, and as a member of the ''[[Organic Syntheses]]'' Board of Editors from 1980 to 1988.<ref name="orgsyn"/> He served as editor (along with [[Scott E. Denmark]]) of the three volume series ''Lewis Base Catalysis in Organic Synthesis.''<ref name="CHCC"/><ref name=Lewis_Base_Catalysis_in_Organic_Synthesis>{{cite book | title=Lewis Base Catalysis in Organic Synthesis | year=2016| doi=10.1002/9783527675142| isbn=9783527675142| editor1-last=Vedejs| editor1-first=Edwin| editor2-last=Denmark| editor2-first=Scott E}}</ref> Over the course of his 45 years in academia, he mentored over 80 doctoral students, and numerous post-doctoral fellows and undergraduates.<ref name="orgsyn"/>

==Awards and honors==

*Alexander von Humboldt Senior Scientist Award, 1984<ref name="CHCC"/>
*Member of the [[Latvian Academy of Sciences]], 1992<ref name ="Member of the Latvian Academy of Sciences">{{cite web | title=Member of the Latvian Academy of Sciences | url=http://www.lza.lv/images/stories/YearBook_2010-2011.pdf | pages=82 | access-date=2020-03-28 | archive-date=2015-07-17 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150717172910/http://www.lza.lv/images/stories/YearBook_2010-2011.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref>
*Paul Walden Medal, 1997<ref name="orgsyn"/>
*Herbert C. Brown Award for Creative Research in Synthetic Methods, 2004<ref name="CHCC"/>
*Grand Medal of the Latvian Academy of Sciences, 2005<ref name ="CHCC"/>
*[[Order of the Three Stars]], Republic of Latvia, 2006<ref name="CHCC"/><ref name ="Order of Three Stars">{{cite web | title=Order of Three Stars | url=https://www.president.lv/storage/kcfinder/files/tzo_2019.pdf | pages=99 | access-date=2020-03-14 | archive-date=2020-05-09 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200509233206/https://www.president.lv/storage/kcfinder/files/tzo_2019.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref>
